title: Translates of Poincaré series fill the rows: a Petersson-type second moment along a Bessel subgroup
summary: Unit 148 (the folder New/Filling) proves the filling theorem used for Theorem B (enough forms): for admissible data D, every nonzero constant c and every subspace F of the rows, some element s of the finite level group 𝖦 = ∏ GL over the residue fields at the chosen places above g = q₀q₁ makes the preimage of F under the composite (|𝖦| e₀ s) ∘ 𝒫 ∘ (c·E) have dimension at most ((1 + dim F/dim rows)/2 + b⁻²)·dim Col, where 𝒫 is the Poincaré series built from cut Bessel functions along the Bessel subgroup S = 𝖴𝖧 of the unitary group of V = H^ϱ ⊕ X₀ ⊕ Ez, e₀ the projection to the rows and E the projection onto the ramified columns (`Data.ramifiedColumns_fill_rows`). The proof is a second-moment (Petersson-type) argument: the mean over s of the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of 𝒫*s𝒫 is unfolded into sums of amplitudes over rational elements γ grouped by double cosets (classes c, c') and by their reductions s modulo g; amplitude sums vanish unless the unipotent characters agree, degenerate terms and incoherent pairs are negligible by discriminant gains, lattice counts and a weighted Schur test, the main term is bounded nearly sharply by positive kernels of local Bessel integrals at finitely many places and a sieve (one-sided Poisson summation), and a variance inequality turns the moment bound into the spreading statement. Chunk 148-a holds the set-up and the first layer: the record `Filling` of the data and its standing hypotheses `IsAdmissible`; abstract sieve systems and Bessel systems; the groups 𝖴, 𝖴⁰, 𝖧, 𝖲, the classes, terms, amplitudes and constants; dictionaries between rational, finite adelic and real coordinates; links of frames (Lagrangian, invariant under 𝖴 on both sides); Siegel's lemma for hermitian lattices and a convergent height zeta function of subspaces; strong approximation for 𝖴; normal forms and levels of terms; the bound of the index of a determinant of pairings by agreeing characters; box partitions (cutoffs) for the arithmetic unipotent groups 𝖴_c(g) and the frame-counting bound; the exact covolume of 𝖴_c(g); and convergence, change of weight, moves, vanishing for disagreeing characters and the identity term of the amplitude sums.

members.name: latMiddleGram
members.text: For a commutative ring R (implicit), a shape 𝔰 and an element N of R: latMiddleGram(𝔰, N) is the square matrix over R indexed by κ ⊔ {z} with diagonal entries 1 at the indices i ≠ k₀ of κ, 0 at k₀ and −N at z, entries −1 at the two positions (k₀, z) and (z, k₀), and 0 elsewhere. It is the Gram matrix of X₀ ⊕ Ez (form 1 on X₀, −N at z) in the basis x_i (i ≠ k₀), v, z, where v = x_{k₀}/π + z/N (π = conj(π̄); this is the k₀-column of the lattice basis besselLatticeBasis(𝔰, π̄), whose k₀-entry is conj(π̄)⁻¹; any v = x_{k₀}/p + z/N with p·p̄ = N gives the same Gram matrix, and the Lean comment writes x_{k₀}/π̄) is isotropic, h(v, z) = −1 and h(z, z) = −N (N = π π̄).

members.name: middleBaseChange
members.text: For a shape 𝔰 and a unit p of a commutative ring R with involution: middleBaseChange(𝔰, p) is the (κ ⊔ {z}) × κ matrix over R whose rows indexed by κ form the diagonal matrix with p̄ at k₀ and 1 elsewhere, and whose row z has the entry −p⁻¹ in column k₀ and 0 elsewhere. Its columns are the orthonormal vectors x_i of X₀ written in the basis x_i (i ≠ k₀), v, z of X₀ ⊕ Ez, where v = x_{k₀}/p̄ + z/(p p̄): x_{k₀} = p̄ v − z/p.

members.name: besselLatticeBasis
members.text: For a commutative ring R with involution, a shape 𝔰 and a unit p of R: besselLatticeBasis(𝔰, p) is the invertible matrix in GL over R indexed by the basis of the whole space V = H^ϱ ⊕ X₀ ⊕ Ez that is the identity on the vectors e_a and e*_a and, on X₀ ⊕ Ez, has the columns x_i (i ∈ κ, i ≠ k₀), v = x_{k₀}/p̄ + z/(p p̄) in the place of x_{k₀}, and z. So its columns are e_a; x_i (i ≠ k₀), v, z; e*_a in standard coordinates. (The definition supplies the inverse, block diagonal with middleBaseChange(𝔰, p) on X₀, and checks both products by simp and grind.)

members.name: frameDisc
members.text: For a commutative ring R with involution, a shape 𝔰 (implicit), N ∈ R and a square matrix Z of size ϱ+1 over R: frameDisc(N, Z) = det Z · conj(det Z) − N²·D_ϱ(Z)·conj(D_ϱ(Z)), where D_ϱ(Z) is the leading principal minor of order ϱ (the determinant of the upper left ϱ × ϱ block). For Z = Z(γ) this is the Gram discriminant 𝗀(γ) = |D_{ϱ+1}|² − N²|D_ϱ|².

members.name: SieveSystem
members.text: For types C and U, where C is a commutative ring with a measure and U a topological space, maps u : C → U and ι : U → C, a length n ∈ ℕ, forms J_i(p, q) ∈ ℂ (i ∈ ℕ, p, q : ℕ → U sequences), a function ψ : C → ℂ, a real number En, real head bounds Λ_i(p) and a function β : C → ℝ, SieveSystem(u, ι, n, J, ψ, En, Λ, β) is the record of the following facts. (psi_zero) ψ(0) = 1. (step) For every i ≤ n, all sequences p, q and every ξ ∈ C, the function f(c) = ψ(ξc)·J_{i+1}(p[i ↦ u(c)], q[i ↦ u(c)]) is integrable on C, ∫f = J_i(p, q) when ξ = 0, and |∫f| ≤ β(ξ)·Λ_i(p)·Λ_i(q) when ξ is a unit of C; here p[i ↦ x] is p with entry i replaced by x. (posSemidef) For every finite type κ, every family a : κ → (ℕ → U) and t ∈ U with a_k(n) = t for all k, the matrix (J_{n+1}(a_k, a_l))_{k,l} is positive semidefinite. (continuous) (p, q) ↦ J_{n+1}(p, q) is continuous. (norm_bot_le) |J_0(p, q)| ≤ En for all p, q. (off_diagonal) For every i < n and all p, q such that ξ = ι(p_i) − ι(q_i) is a unit, |J_{i+1}(p, q)| ≤ β(ξ)·Λ_{i+1}(p)·Λ_{i+1}(q).

members.text: Let C be a commutative ring with a measure that is s-finite, U a topological space, τ a finite type, and K = SieveSystem(u, ι, n, J, ψ, En, Λ, β) a sieve system on C (with u : C → U, ι : U → C, n, J, ψ, En, Λ, β implicit). Let ι' : ℂˣ → ℂ and Λ' be given (implicit), and for each v ∈ τ forms J'_v, a bound En'_v and a function γ_v : ℂ → ℝ such that H_v = SieveSystem(unitOrOne, ι', n, J'_v, wave, En'_v, Λ', γ_v) is a sieve system on ℂ (unitOrOne(c) = c if c ≠ 0, else 1; wave(c) = exp(c − c̄)). Then the product is a sieve system on the ring (τ → ℂ) × C with its product measure: SieveSystem(u⁺, ι⁺, n, J⁺, ψ⁺, En⁺, Λ⁺, β⁺) holds for u⁺(x) = ((unitOrOne(x_v))_v, u(x_C)), ι⁺(y) = ((ι'(y_v))_v, ι(y_U)), J⁺_i(p, q) = (∏_v J'_{v,i}(p_v, q_v))·J_i(p_C, q_C), ψ⁺(x) = (∏_v wave(x_v))·ψ(x_C), En⁺ = (∏_v En'_v)·En, Λ⁺_i(p) = (∏_v Λ'_i(p_v))·Λ_i(p_C) and β⁺(x) = (∏_v γ_v(x_v))·β(x_C); here p_v and p_C are the sequences of v-components and of C-components of a sequence p in (τ → ℂˣ) × U.

lemma SieveSystem.step_sum (K : SieveSystem u ι n J ψ En Λ β) {i} (hi : i ≤ n) (a : τ → _) :
  let F c := ∑ p, ∑ q, J (i + 1) (update (a p) i (u c)) (update (a q) i (u c))
  Integrable F ∧ ∫ c, F c = ∑ p, ∑ q, J i (a p) (a q) ∧ ∀ ξ, IsUnit ξ → ‖∫ c, ψ (ξ * c) * F c‖ ≤
    β ξ * (∑ p, Λ i (a p)) ^ 2

members.name: finHeadWeight
members.text: For a semilocal field A (a finite product of non-archimedean local fields, with compact open subring O, `SemilocalField`), natural numbers K and i and a sequence p : ℕ → Aˣ of units: finHeadWeight(K, i, p) = ∏_{l < i} w_l with D_l = p₀ p₁ ⋯ p_l and w_l = √(genIndex(D_l))^K if D_l ∈ O, w_l = 0 otherwise; here genIndex(D) is the inverse module of D, which for D ∈ O equals the index [O : D·O]. So it is the product of [O : D_l O]^{K/2}, taken to be 0 as soon as some D_l is not integral.

members.name: exists_mem_besselU_eq_eichlerMap
members.text: Let A be a commutative ring with involution, 𝔰 a shape, T a Gram matrix on V_ϱ over A such that J = T.splitGram is hermitian and invertible, and τ ∈ A with τ + τ̄ = 1 (`TraceOne A`). Let a ∈ {0, …, ϱ}, j ∈ A^{ϱ+1} with j_b = 0 for all b ≥ a (hypothesis l), r ∈ A, v a vector of the whole space and m = v̄ᵀJ = h(v, ·) (hypothesis Z) with m(f_b) = 0 for all frame vectors f_b, b < a (hypothesis H). Then there is u in the unipotent group 𝖴 = besselU(T) with σ(u) = r·∑_{b ≥ 1} m(f_b)·j_{b−1} (σ = simpleRootSum, the sum of the entries of u just above the diagonal on the frame) and whose matrix is the Eichler map E(x, v, ς): w ↦ w + x·h(v, w) − (v + ςx)·h(x, w), for x = r·(f j) = r·∑_b j_b f_b and ς = τ·h(v, v). (The census also lists the file's section variables C, U, τ, u, A, [CommRing C], [MeasureSpace C], [TopologicalSpace U], [Fintype τ], [CommRing A]: the statement contains the letters u and τ only as a bound variable and inside `TraceOne.τ`.)

members.name: BesselSystem
members.text: For a shape 𝔰, a real number b and a natural number f: a Bessel system BesselSystem(𝔰, b, f) is a record of a nonempty finite type I; a pair W of continuous functions W_full, W_cut : G₁ → ℂ^I; a real number deg > 0; a unitary representation rep of U(κ) on ℂ^I with IsCutPair(b, f, rep, W); irreducibility: every matrix M commuting with all rep(h) is scalar; Schur bounds: HasSchurBound(W_full, rep, P, deg⁻¹·|I|) for every P ≥ b⁵; 8r ≤ b (r the rank of V); and band limits: forms bandLimit with HasBandLimits(b, W_cut, deg, bandLimit). (The census also lists the section variables I, W, deg, which the structure's own fields shadow.)

members.name: Filling
members.text: For a number field E with a CM type (`Field E`, `CMType E`) and a shape 𝔰, filling data S : Filling(E, 𝔰) is a record of: a natural number N; two natural numbers q₀ = levelPrime 0 and q₁ = levelPrime 1; a finite idele π̄ = piBar ∈ (𝔸_f)ˣ; an integer ϖ ∈ 𝓞_E; a real number b; for i = 0, 1 a finite set chosenPlaces(i) of finite places of E; a subgroup K_c = columnLevel of the finite adelic unitary group G_f(κ) of X₀ that is a level (open, inside G_f ∩ GL_κ(Ô)) and satisfies U(X₀)(E) ∩ g K_c g⁻¹ = 1 for every g (aut_columnLevel); and at every infinite place v a Bessel system besselSys(v) : BesselSystem(𝔰, b, f), f the number of infinite places of E; subject to: π̄·conj(π̄) = N; N is prime; at every finite place w, π̄ is a unit at w, or w has norm N and π̄ is a unit at w̄; π̄ ∈ Ô; each q_i is a prime different from N with b^10 ≤ q_i ≤ b^11; every chosen place above q_i has norm q_i; the chosen places for i = 0 and i = 1 are distinct (the map from Σ_i chosenPlaces(i) to the places is injective), and no conjugate w̄ of a chosen place w is chosen; for every r ∈ Ô, g = q₀q₁ divides r iff r and r̄ reduce to 0 modulo every chosen place; each chosenPlaces(i) has f elements; ϖ̄ = −ϖ and the different of E is the ideal (ϖ); 10⁵ ≤ ϱ; 2^{−ϱ} ≤ b^{−6}; (ϱ+1)·[E : ℚ] ≤ 2^{2ϱ}; 1000(2ϱ+2)⁹ ≤ k and 1000(2ϱ+2) ≤ k (k = |κ|); k ≤ f; (200·f·k·rd_E)^{1000} ≤ b (rd_E the root discriminant); f ≤ b/1000; k ≤ b; rd_E ≤ b; ϱ+1 ≤ b; 1000 ≤ b; 1 ≤ b; b^19 ≤ q₀q₁ ≤ b^23; 5 ≤ N; and, with n = ϱ+1, 10^10·n⁴ ≤ n⁶, 3n⁶ + 12 ≤ n⁷ and n⁷ ≤ k.

members.name: Filling.IsBoxPartition
members.text: For filling data S (over a CM number field E with its CM type, for a shape 𝔰; E and 𝔰 implicit), a class c and a function ω from archimedean points y = (y_v)_v ∈ ∏_v G₁ to [0, ∞]: IsBoxPartition(S, c, ω) holds iff ω is measurable; for all y and v, if ω(y) ≠ 0 and InCut(y_v, b) then y_v ∈ frameBox(boxSize(S)); for every y and every a : 𝖴_c(g) → [0, ∞] whose sum over each coset 𝖴⁰_c(g)γ is 1 (∑_{u ∈ 𝖴⁰_c(g)} a(uγ) = 1 for all γ), ∑_{γ ∈ 𝖴_c(g)} a(γ)·ω(ratToInf(γ)·y) = 1; ω ≤ 1; and ω(s·y) = ω(y) whenever s_v ∈ 𝖴⁰ ⊔ 𝖧 at every infinite place v (left invariance under 𝖴⁰ and 𝖧 at infinity).

members.name: Filling.exists_cutoff_classUnip
members.text: Let S be filling data over E for 𝔰, c a class (implicit) and K a subgroup of 𝖴_c(g) = classUnip(S, c). Let Γ be the image of K in ∏_v G₁ under ratToInf(S). members.name: Filling.siegel_lemma
members.text: Siegel's lemma (Bombieri–Vaaler) for hermitian lattices. Let E be a stably unramified CM field with f infinite places and root discriminant rd_E, κ a finite set, u ∈ G_f(κ) (the finite adelic unitary group of the standard form), T a subspace of E^κ and s a natural number with dim T + s = |κ| (hs). Then there is an s × κ matrix X over E with rows X_1, …, X_s such that T is the orthogonal complement of the rows (T = ker(x ↦ (∑_j conj(X_ij) x_j)_i)), every row is a nonzero vector of the lattice E^κ ∩ uÔ^κ (the base lattice of the standard space moved by (1, u)), and (∏_i ‖X_i‖)^{2f} ≤ (8fs·rd_E)^{fs}·d(T), where ‖X_i‖ is the Euclidean norm of (Φ_v(X_ij))_{v,j} over all infinite places and d(T) = sublatticeDisc(u, T) is the discriminant of T ∩ uÔ^κ.

lemma norm_sq_middle_part_eq {D t} (h : S.frameProducts γ *ᵥ y = Pi.single 𝔰.top D) (e :
  frameImage γ.1.1 *ᵥ y = t) : ((∀ a, t (eStar a) = 0) ∧ -(S.N * t 𝔰.z) = D) ∧
  ∀ v, let s := S.N * ∑ i, ‖Φ v (t (𝔰.indexX₀ i))‖ ^ 2
  s = ‖Φ v D‖ ^ 2 - (S.N * ‖Φ v (y 𝔰.top)‖) ^ 2 ∧ (s ≤ 0 → ∃ x, frameImage 1 *ᵥ x = t)

members.name: Filling.liouville_gram
members.text: Liouville inequality for Gram determinants. Let E be a stably unramified CM field, σ, τ finite, Q a τ × τ matrix over E that is totally positive definite (Φ_w(Q) positive definite at every infinite place w; hQ), a, b τ × σ matrices over E with det(aᴴQb) ≠ 0 (h), v, v' ∈ GL_σ(𝔸_f), and x a real number with x ≥ 0 (hx) such that x ≤ [δ] whenever δ = det(vᴴ·(aᴴQb)·v') is a unit of 𝔸_f (i). Then x² ≤ [det v]²·|N(det aᴴQa)|·|N(det bᴴQb)|·[det v']², N the norm to ℚ and [·] = genIndex.

lemma le_genIndex_det_of_fixesNormAtLeast [StablyUnram E] {k x} (s :
  S'.Agrees (S'.reduction k)) {t : Matrix 𝔰.BesselIndex τ' _} {P} (ht : IsIntMatrix (Ô E) t)
  (i : (framePair k.1)ᴴ * t = P) (z : P.submatrix (.map castSucc castSucc) id = 0) (ρ :
  τ' ≃ Unit ⊕ Unit) : let g := .map (fun _ ↦ 𝔰.top) (fun _ ↦ 𝔰.top) ∘ ρ
  IsUnit (P.submatrix g id).det → S'.FixesNormAtLeast (S'.reduction k) x → x ≤
    genIndex (P.submatrix g id).det

members.name: Filling.energy_le_of_level_pairs
members.text: Lemma (incoherent and degenerate pairs are negligible). Let E be stably unramified and S admissible, and use the cut Bessel functions. Let C, w be reals with 0 ≤ C and 0 ≤ w, Ω ⊆ 𝖦, T a stable set of rational points, X ≠ 0 a natural number such that every s ∈ Ω satisfies FixesNormAtLeast(S, s, X) (s fixes, modulo chosen places of total norm ≥ X, a nonzero vector of the span of the frame), 𝖽₁ ≤ C (𝖽₁ = besselEnergy(S)), and τ²⁰𝖽₁ ≤ C if some γ ∈ T over some (c, s, c') with s ∈ Ω is in normal form of level 0. Let j ∈ {0, …, ϱ+1} with HasLevel(S, j, γ) for all γ ∈ T, R a set of links such that τ¹²/X^k·𝖽 ≤ C whenever ϱ < j and some link is not in R (𝖽 = mainEnergy(S)), and assume linkEnergy(T, Ω, R) ≤ w·ν². Then energy(amplitudeSum(S, T), Ω) ≤ w + C/b³⁰/4^{ϱ+1−j} (τ = tailScale(S), ν = unipCovolume(S)).

Let 0 ≤ C, 0 ≤ w, Ω ⊆ 𝖦, T stable, X ≠ 0 with FixesNormAtLeast(S, s, X) for all s ∈ Ω, 𝖽₁ ≤ C, τ²⁰𝖽₁ ≤ C if some γ ∈ T over some (c, s, c') with s ∈ Ω is in normal form of level 0; let R be a set of links with τ¹²/X^k·𝖽 ≤ C if some link is not in R, and assume that the link energy of the terms of T with 𝗀 ≠ 0, for the cut Bessel functions, is linkEnergy(T ∩ {γ : termDisc(S, γ) ≠ 0}, Ω, R) ≤ w·ν². Then for the full Bessel functions energy(amplitudeSum(S, T), Ω) ≤ (1 + b⁻⁴)²·w + b⁻¹²·C.

members.name: Data.exists_last_stage_map
members.text: Lemma (last step of the seesaw). For data D of parameters P and M with e : D.m = M (m the number of lifts), there is a ℂ-linear map R from Stage(D, M) (smooth algebraic forms on X_M of weight (κ, e_M)) to the algebraic forms on Y_M such that (1) for every twist ϑ, finitely supported coefficients Ψ on translations, form y of principal level on Y₀ and column φ: if liftChainY(ϑ, M, y) = R(chainComb(ϑ, Ψ, translateDatum, M, φ)) then ι(ϑ, y) = Bμ(ϑ, Ψ, φ); and (2) for every linear functional t on Weyl coordinates there is C ∈ ℂ such that for every form x on Y_M, every ψ ∈ Stage(D, M) and every function F on the adelic group of Y_M with F(inclX(k)) = algFormCoeff(1, t, ψ)(blockEmb(k, 1)) for all k (lastGrading(D, e).inclX), the integral of F·x̄ over the quotient (ratBessel(lastGrading(D, e)).qms) equals C·⟨x, Rψ⟩.

members.name: Filling.one_sided_poisson
members.text: Lemma (iterated one-sided Poisson summation). Let S be admissible, T a finite set of finite places, A a finite set of units of E with t, t⁻¹ integral outside T for t ∈ A, and g⁻¹ integral outside T. Let n ∈ ℕ and let K be a sieve system (SieveSystem) of depth n on ℂ^f × ∏_{w∈T} E_w with forms J_i and unit map u. The map u replaces each zero complex coordinate by 1. It keeps the finite tuple when all its coordinates are nonzero and sends the whole tuple to 1 otherwise. The system uses the map p ↦ (p_∞⁻¹, ratToPlaces(T)(g⁻¹)·p_T⁻¹), character x ↦ ∏_v wave(x_v)·charOnPlaces(S, T)(x_T), bottom bound En, weights Λ and frequency bound β (so J_i integrates J_{i+1} over a common entry, J_{n+1} is continuous and positive on equal entries, |J₀| ≤ En, and unit frequencies and unequal entries are bounded by β·Λ·Λ). Let Γ, ε be reals with ε ≥ 0, Λ ≥ 0, and assume: for every a and every c = (c_v) with |c_v|⁻¹ ≤ |κ_v|/g for all v and every finite set X of nonzero T-integers, Σ_{y∈X} β(ratPoint(T, (c_v/frameScaleSq(S, v, a))_v, y)) ≤ ε. Put hd(i, p, t, a) = the unit image of ratPoint(T, (frameScaleSq(S, v, a))_v, padTuple(p, t, a)) for p : Fin i → A and t ∈ Eˣ, and c_a = vol(Ô)/∏_v frameScaleSq(S, v, a)². If (Σ_p Λ_i(hd(i, p, 1)))² ≤ Γ·∏_{a<i} c_a for every i ≤ n, then for every i ≤ n and every V ⊆ A: Re Σ_{t∈V} Σ_p Σ_q J_{i+1}(hd(i, p, t), hd(i, q, t)) ≤ (∏_{a≤i} c_a)·(En + (2i+1)·Γ·ε), p, q over Fin i → A.

members.text: Definition (structure). For the filling data S, a hermitian space V over E with signs ε and point x (`Space`), families l (Harish-Chandra parameters) and kw (weights) indexed by the infinite places, a grading Y of V with constant N and η ∈ U(X₀)(𝔸_f), Fits(S, V, l, kw, Y, η) consists of: (isBessel) at each infinite place v the Bessel system of S has type (l_v, kw_v) (IsBessel: its degree is Weyl's dimension of l_v, the full Bessel function transforms under U(X₀) through the Schur matrix of weight kw_v after an invertible change of coordinates, and it is fixed by right integration against the discrete-series kernel of l_v); (index_eq) the indexing of Y is the standard one, besselIndexEquiv; (isIdempotentKernel) typeKernel(l, ε) is an idempotent kernel; (point_eq) there is an integral k ≡ 1 at every chosen place and a finite idele u with x_f = u·toBesselH(N, η)·latBasis(S)·k; (central) η commutes with every element of U(X₀)(𝔸_f).

lemma integral_poincare [StablyUnram E]
    {Δ q y} (h : Δ ≤ V.Γ) (k : V.IsForm q y) : let F := y * X.poincare φ Δ

members.name: Filling.lintegral_boxCutoff_le_of_average
members.text: Lemma (averaging). Let S be admissible, c a class, (X, m) a measurable space with an s-finite measure m, s : X → (infinite places → G₁) measurable with s(x)_v ∈ 𝖴⁰ for all x, v; F : G_∞ → [0, ∞] measurable and left invariant under 𝖴⁰_c(g) (F(u_∞·y) = F(y) for u ∈ classUnip₀(S, c)); B ⊆ X with 1 ≤ m(B); C ∈ [0, ∞] such that for every u ∈ G_∞ with all u_v ∈ 𝖴⁰ and every y ∈ boxedPoints(S): ∫_B F(u·s(x)·y) dm(x) ≤ C. Then ∫ boxCutoff(S, c, y) · ∏_v ‖W_v^cut(y_v)‖² · F(y) dy ≤ C · (ν · #BesselCoord(S)), with ν = unipCovolume(S) and #BesselCoord(S) = ∏_v #I_v.

members.name: IntegralPlace.exists_isLatticeLevel
members.text: Lemma. At a finite place with integers R (A semilocal with involution and integral place structure P), let N ∈ R with N̄ = N (the whole Gram matrix of latMiddleGram(𝔰, N) hermitian invertible), g a unit with g ∈ R and ḡ = g, and k = |ι| + 2m + 1. Then there is a level F' of latMiddleGram(𝔰, N) with m pairs which is a lattice level (IsLatticeLevel(P, F')) and has F'.g = g.

members.name: IntegralPlace.IsStdLevel.gauge
members.text: Definition. For a standard level F and a unit α with α ∈ R and ᾱ = α (by default α = 1): the gauge of depth α of F (a `Gauge`): a vector x has size j if α^j·x ∈ R, and Λ = 2/md(α); the construction verifies the bounds required of a gauge (compact size sets, the level's data of size 1, Λ ≥ 2 and its powers bounding moduli, volumes, cone masses and the integrals of the volume majorant).

members.name: Filling.terms_of_class_spec
members.text: Lemma. Let j ∈ {0, …, ϱ+1}, classes c, c', s ∈ 𝖦 and γ ∈ G(E) with γ ∈ termsOver(S, c, s, c') (h_c⁻¹γh_c' ∈ K with reduction s) and HasLevel(S, j, γ). Then every δ in the double coset 𝖴⁰_c(g)·γ·𝖴⁰_c'(g) (𝖴⁰_c(g) = classUnip₀(S, c)) satisfies: HasLevel(S, j, δ); frameProducts(S, δ) = frameProducts(S, γ) (the matrix Z(·) of products h(f_a, ·f_b) with the frame f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)); δ ∈ termsOver(S, c, s, c'); and for every column index i the i-th column of (frameMiddle(k_δ) − frameMiddle(k_γ))ᴴ lies in gIdele(S)·colLattice(Ô_E, xRows(Z_lat(k_γ))ᴴ), where k_δ = termPosition(S, c, c', δ) = h_c⁻¹δh_c', frameMiddle(k) are the X₀ ⊕ Ez rows of k f, Z_lat(k) is the frame Gram matrix of k for the lattice form latMiddle(S), xRows takes its first ϱ rows, colLattice(Ô_E, M) is the Ô_E-span of the columns of M and gIdele(S) is g = q₀q₁ as a finite idele.

members.name: Filling.tsum_schurIntegral_le
members.text: Lemma (Schur test on a thin class). Let E be stably unramified and S admissible; let j ∈ {0, …, ϱ+1}, classes c, c', s ∈ 𝖦 and γ ∈ G(E) with γ ∈ termsOver(S, c, s, c') and HasLevel(S, j, γ). Then Σ_{δ ∈ 𝖴⁰_c(g)γ𝖴⁰_c'(g)} schurIntegral(S, c, c', δ) ≤ ν · #BesselCoord(S) · τ² · (b⁴g)^{−min(ϱ, j)·k·f} · (i/√D)^{k+1}, where i = xRowsIndex(S, j, termPosition(S, c, c', γ)) (the index of the Ô-span of the conjugated first min(j, ϱ) rows of Z(h_c⁻¹γh_c') in that of its first ϱ rows), D = minorNorm(S, j, γ) (|N_{E/ℚ}(D_j(Z(γ)))|, divided by N^{2f} when j = ϱ+1), τ = tailScale(S) = b^{kf/4}, ν = unipCovolume(S), g = q₀q₁, k = |κ| and f the number of infinite places.

lemma IsFillingLevel.correlation_smul_eq_cosetAmplitude [S.IsAdmissible] [Side] {σ p c c'} {Z :
  F.IntermediateGroup} {k : S.latStabilizer} (u : σ ∈ GT 𝔰.ϱ) (o : S.IsIntegralOff T
  (S.termPosition c c' (weylElem 𝔰.ϱ p * σ))) {a b : Z.Cosets} (e : (S.toPlaces T k)⁻¹ * a.out.1 *
  b.out.1⁻¹ ∈ F.congGroup) : let q := Units.map (ratToPlaces T) ∘ p; let γ := weylElem 𝔰.ϱ p * σ
    F.correlation Z q (S.toPlaces T (S.termPosition c c' σ))⁻¹ (a, b) • besselCorrelation volume
      (.toLp 2 <| S.besselFn ·) (S.ratToInf γ) = (F.headDensity 𝔰.ϱ q 1).toReal •
      F.groupMeasure.real F.congGroup • S.cosetAmplitude T c (S.reduction k) c' γ

members.name: IntegralPlace.phase
members.text: At a finite place: A a semilocal field with involution and integral place structure P (integers R, additive character ψ, modulus md), T a middle form with invertible hermitian whole Gram matrix J. Definition. For a unit g and z in the unitary group U(J): phase(g, z) = ψ(g⁻¹·σ(u)) if z ∈ u·K(g) for some u ∈ 𝖴 (u a chosen such element; σ(u) = simpleRootSum(u), the sum of the entries at the simple roots of the frame block; K(g) = unitaryLevel(R, g, J)), and 0 if z ∉ 𝖴·K(g). This is the finite Bessel function χ_g.

members.text: At a finite place: A a semilocal field with involution and integral place structure P (integers R, additive character ψ, modulus md), T a middle form with invertible hermitian whole Gram matrix J. For a standard level and Z ∈ IntermediateGroup(F), y ↦ besselVector(Z, y) is a cut Bessel vector for F (IsCut): it is strongly measurable and bounded by a uniform finite constant — ‖W_Z(y)‖ ≤ √#(K(g)∖Z) for every y, each of its coset coordinates being a phase of modulus at most 1 (not a bound by 1 on the Euclidean norm) —, it transforms under 𝖴 by W_Z(uy) = ψ(g⁻¹σ(u))·W_Z(y) (σ the superdiagonal sum of the frame block), and it is nonzero only at points y with u·y in the box K for some u ∈ 𝖴.

members.text: At a finite place: A a semilocal field with involution and an integral place structure P (integers R, character ψ, modulus md), T a middle form over A with invertible hermitian split Gram matrix J, F a standard level of T (h : IsStdLevel F) with m + 1 further pairs, and Z ∈ IntermediateGroup(F). Lemma. Let j ≤ ϱ (hj: a section hypothesis that the statement uses in its index ⟨j, by lia⟩, so Lean binds it although the census does not list it), t with (ht) t + 10¹⁰n⁴ ≤ k (n = ϱ + 1, k = k(𝔰)), K with (hK) 10¹⁰n⁴ ≤ K, sequences of units p, q, a unit ξ of A, and ω such that (H) either ω(x) = ψ(ξ·frameGram(x)_{jj}) — the j-th diagonal entry, counting from 0 (the docstring counts from 1 and writes j+1) — or j = i + 1, ω = 1 and ξ = F.g⁻¹(p_i⁻¹ − q_i⁻¹) for some i. For parameters P, admissible data D for P and a unit c ∈ ℂ^×, put for s ∈ 𝖦_D B_s = goodProjTranslate(D, s) ∘ poincare(D) ∘ (c·ramifyingOp(D, piPlaces(D))) : Column(D) → rows(D), where goodProjTranslate(D, s)(y) = #𝖦_D · e₀(D)·(s·y) (s acting on principalForms(D, Y₀(D)) through the principal representation, e₀(D) ∈ ℂ[𝖦_D] the good idempotent, whose image is rows(D)), poincare(D) = 𝒫_D is the Poincaré series map, and ramifyingOp(D, piPlaces(D)) = ∏_{w | π} (1 − z_w) on Column(D), z_w the translation by the scalar centralGen(D, w), the product over all finite places w dividing π = π(D). Then the family (B_s)_{s∈𝖦_D} is spread with defect b_D⁻² (`IsSpread`): for every ℂ-subspace F of rows(D), with φ = dim F / dim rows(D) (read as 0 when dim rows(D) = 0), there is s ∈ 𝖦_D with dim_ℂ {ψ ∈ Column(D) : B_s(ψ) ∈ F} ≤ ((1 + φ)/2 + b_D⁻²)·dim_ℂ Column(D).

Let f be a [0, ∞]-valued function on the vectors over LocProd(T) (indexed by BesselIndex(𝔰)), s a finite set of pairs z = (c_z, y_z) of a class of S and a vector y_z ∈ E^κ, t ∈ E with (ht) N(S)² < |Φ_v(t)|² for every infinite place v, and c : Classes(S) × E^κ → ℝ_{≥0}. members.name: Filling.IsFillingLevel.exists_finite_sieveSystem
members.text: Lemma. Let E be a number field with a CM structure and Weil data, 𝔰 a shape, S admissible filling data over E of shape 𝔰, T a finite set of finite places of E stable under conjugation, P an integral place structure on LocProd(T) (an implicit argument, also an instance), F a level with hF : IsFillingLevel(S, T, F), Sg a finite set of chosen places of S above q₀(S), d frame-vector data (for each chosen place w above q₀(S): a flag and a nonzero vector over 𝔽_w), and suppose (an instance) gIdele(S)⁻¹ is integral outside T. Then there is an intermediate group Z of F such that (i) toPlaces(S, T, k) ∈ Z for every k ∈ latStabilizer(S) with reduction(S, k) ∈ fixingSet(S, Sg, d), and (ii) for every open additive subgroup L of LocProd(T) that is compact, the kernels J(j, p, q) = (floorForm(F, j, p, q, besselVector(Z), 1) if j ≤ ϱ, topKernel(L, Z, p, q)/vol(L) if j = ϱ + 1)/massRatio(Z) form a sieve system SieveSystem(unitOrOne, x ↦ g(S)_T⁻¹·x⁻¹, ϱ, J, charOnPlaces(S, T), (1 + b(S)⁻⁶)/(b(S)^{6k(𝔰)})^{#Sg}, finHeadWeight(n(𝔰)⁶), frequencyGain(S, T)). Unfolded, with Λ = finHeadWeight(n⁶) and β = frequencyGain(S, T): ψ = charOnPlaces(S, T) has ψ(0) = 1; for i ≤ ϱ and sequences p, q of units and ξ ∈ LocProd(T), the function c ↦ ψ(ξc)·J(i+1, p[i ↦ unitOrOne(c)], q[i ↦ unitOrOne(c)]) is integrable, its integral is J(i, p, q) when ξ = 0, and has norm ≤ β(ξ)·Λ(i, p)Λ(i, q) when ξ is a unit; for every finite family of sequences with a common ϱ-th term the matrix of J(ϱ+1) is positive semidefinite; J(ϱ+1) is continuous; ‖J(0, p, q)‖ ≤ (1 + b⁻⁶)/(b^{6k})^{#Sg}; and for i < ϱ, with ξ = g_T⁻¹(p_i⁻¹ − q_i⁻¹) a unit, ‖J(i+1, p, q)‖ ≤ β(ξ)·Λ(i+1, p)Λ(i+1, q).

Let o be either nothing or a place w ∈ Sg, let d assign to every chosen place w above q₀(S) a pair d_w = (a flag, a nonzero vector v_w over the residue field 𝔽_w) (the data of `vectorFixer`), suppose (hT) that g(S)⁻¹ = gIdele(S)⁻¹ is integral at every finite place outside T₀, and suppose (f) that if o = w then T = T₀ ∩ {w, w̄} (for every finite place j: j ∈ T ⟺ j ∈ T₀ and (j = w or j̄ = w)). Let E be a number field with a CM structure, 𝔰 a shape, S filling data over E of shape 𝔰, j ∈ {0, …, ϱ+1} and γ ∈ G(E) of level j (h: HasLevel(S, j, γ) — γ is in normal form of index j, D_j(γ) ≠ 0, and ϱ < j ⟺ 𝗀(γ) ≠ 0). Let r split the indices a ∈ {0, …, ϱ − 1} of the isotropic frame vectors e_a = f_a (a < ϱ) into a < j and a ≥ j, and let P be the matrix with the columns e_a (all a < ϱ), γe_a (a < j), e*_a (j ≤ a < ϱ), z = f_top = f_ϱ and γz — the isotropic frame vectors, their images under γ below j, the dual basis vectors from j on, and z, γz, each of these two once (m = isotropicFramePair(γ) = (e_a | γe_a)_{a<ϱ}, s the columns e*_a, p the pair (z, γz), as in the lets). Put M = P*·J·P + diag(0, N(S)·1), N(S) added on the diagonal of the last block (the columns e*_a, z, γz). Then [det M] = (N(S)^{2f}·minorNorm(S, j, γ))². (Notation: T = ratMiddle(S) is the Gram matrix of the rational middle form X₀ ⊕ Ez with z of square h(z, z) = −N(S) (T = middleGram(N(S)): 1 on X₀ and −N(S) at z), J = ratGram(S) its split Gram matrix on BesselIndex(𝔰); Z(γ) = frameProducts(S, γ); D_j(γ) = leadingMinor(Z(γ), j); 𝗀(γ) = termDisc(S, γ); link(γ) ⊆ (X₀ ⊕ Ez)² is the image under linkMatrix(γ) of the J-orthogonal of the isotropic frame pair (f_a, γf_a); zFormPair(T) = diag(T_z, T_z) takes the z-pairing in both halves; linkMetric(S) = ½·diag(T, T) + N(S)⁻¹·zFormPair(T)*zFormPair(T), the diagonal matrix with 1/2 at the X₀-coordinates and −N(S)/2 + N(S) = N(S)/2 at the two z-coordinates; linkDiscSq(S, v, e) = |N_{E/ℚ}(det(v*·linkMetric(S)·v))|·[det e]², [·] the generalised index of a finite adele; minorNorm(S, j, γ) = |N_{E/ℚ}(D_j(γ))|/N(S)^{2(j−ϱ)₊f}; termDiscNorm(S, γ) = ∏_v |Φ_v(𝗀(γ))|; HasIntegralLifts(S, c, γ, m): m = linkMatrix(γ)·t·w for a rational t with (isotropic frame pair of γ)*·J·t = 0 and adelic w with classCoord(S, c)·t·w integral; f = f(E) the number of infinite places.)

lemma HasLevel.abs_norm_bordered_det (h :
  S.HasLevel j γ) : let r := sumCompl (@val _ · < j); let m := isotropicFramePair γ
    let f := .map r (r ∘ inl); let s := (diagonal 1).submatrix id (inr ∘ inr ∘ r ∘ inr)
      let p := (framePair γ).submatrix id (.map (fun () ↦ 𝔰.top) fun () ↦ 𝔰.top); let P :=
          ((m.submatrix id f).fromCols
          (s.fromCols p)); let M := Pᴴ * S.ratGram * P + fromBlocks 0 0 0 ((S.N : E) • 1)
          genIndex (finAdeleMat M).det = (S.N ^ (2 * numInfPlaces E) * S.minorNorm j γ) ^ 2

members.text: Lemma (second moment with constant one). Let E be a number field with a CM structure and Weil data, 𝔰 a shape, S admissible filling data over E of shape 𝔰, and V a complex inner product space. imports.text: Minkowski's second theorem: for y ∈ GL_n(𝔸) there are a basis Y_j of E^n and integers x_j with y⁻¹Y_j integral at the finite places, of Euclidean length ≤ 2^{x_j} over all f infinite places, and |det y|_𝔸·4^{f∑x_j} ≤ (8fn·rd_E)^{fn}. literature.verdict: Bombieri–Vaaler Theorem 3 gives the claimed constant after passing from their product body to a joint Euclidean norm and rounding the radii to powers of two.
literature.comparison: Take E CM with f complex places, d=2f, rank n, rd=|disc E|^{1/d} and y∈GL_n(𝔸_E). The vectors form an E-basis. For each column Y_j, y⁻¹Y_j must be finite-integral and have joint Euclidean norm over all infinite places at most 2^{x_j}, with arbitrary integer exponents x_j. In Bombieri–Vaaler’s (3.1) take the finite modules y_v𝒪_vⁿ and, at each complex embedding, the image under y_v of the Euclidean ball of radius 1/√f in ℂⁿ. Each product-body radius r bounds the joint norm by r. In their covolume-one normalization the volume of this body is |det y|_𝔸 · 2^{fn}|disc E|^{−n/2} · (πⁿ/n!)^f f^{−fn}. The factor 2^{fn}|disc E|^{−n/2} comes from the ordinary real covolume (2^{−f}√|disc E|)^n of 𝒪_Eⁿ. Theorem 3 gives (∏r_j)^d vol≤2^{dn} for the E-successive minima. By discreteness the corresponding bounds are attained in the closed bodies. Choose independent vectors successively and set x_j=ceil(log₂ r_j). Dyadic rounding costs at most 2^{dn} after raising the product to d. The resulting bound on |det y|_𝔸·2^{dΣx_j} is 8^{fn}|disc E|^{n/2}(n!)^f f^{fn}/π^{fn}≤(8fn·rd)^{fn}. For rank zero the empty basis has determinant one. A separate verification uses Henk’s real Theorem 1.3 on the joint Euclidean ball. Since an E-subspace of rank j−1 has real Minkowski dimension d(j−1), the (d(j−1)+1)-st real successive minimum supplies the next E-independent vector. Multiplying these block bounds gives the same claimed constant with (fn)!/π^{fn} in the unsimplified joint-ball estimate.
sources: E. Bombieri and J. Vaaler, On Siegel’s lemma, §§II.2–III.1, Theorem 3, equation (3.3), pp. 16–18, adelic successive minima <https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN356556735_0073/LOG_0008.pdf>
M. Henk, Successive minima and lattice points, Theorem 1.3 and its proof in §3, upper bound in Minkowski’s second theorem for general real lattices <https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0204158>

literature.verdict: A quantitative trace-norm neatness lemma for CM ideal levels, requiring an additional argument beyond integral integer level
literature.comparison: Let E have a CM type and at least two infinite places. Let w_i be a finite injective family of finite places and let (2|n|)^[E:ℚ] < ∏_i Nw_i. For any K contained in the principal congruence level there and every finite adelic translate g, the intersection of the rational definite-unitary group with the conjugate level is trivial. Serre's appendix treats finite-order automorphisms of abelian varieties acting trivially modulo an integer N≥3, by a root-of-unity argument in their endomorphism algebra. A product of distinct prime ideals of large norm need not impose that integer-level congruence, and the groups are different. The Lean proof puts tr(γ−1) in the congruence ideal, bounds its absolute norm using unit-modulus roots at the complex places, and forces it to vanish. Positivity of the definite form then forces γ=1. The catalogue note's claim that it bounds all characteristic-polynomial coefficients does not describe these lines.
sources: J.-P. Serre, Rigidité du foncteur de Jacobi d'échelon n ≥ 3, appendix to A. Grothendieck, Séminaire Cartan 13 (1960–61), exposé 17, pp. 17-18–17-20, theorem at p. 17-19. The input is a finite-order automorphism of an abelian variety congruent to 1 modulo an integer. <https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1960-1961__13_2_A4_0.pdf#page=20>

The trace, norm divisibility and final positive-definite argument in the pinned proof. <https://github.com/lsernau/grh-lean/blob/72fead102f663d5c7a407964a13dc0cf9d977207/grh-compact/src/Lib/Shimura/IntegralModel/NeatLevel.lean#L289-L308>

literature.verdict: A one-sided Poisson estimate for a nonnegative integrable function, with local lower semicontinuity replacing global regularity.
literature.comparison: Lean bounds a finite sum of point values by S when every finite partial sum of absolute Fourier coefficients on the dual rational lattice is ≤S. The number field is totally complex. Only the points in the specified finite set need lower semicontinuity. Tate's Theorem 4.1.4 identifies the annihilator of the rational lattice. The Poisson identity is Lemma 4.2.4. Its continuity and uniform periodization hypotheses do not hold for the general Lean input. To pass to the inequality, integrate the periodization on the compact quotient against a nonnegative approximate identity at zero. Its Fourier coefficients are at most one in modulus, and absolute summability bounds the averaged sum by S. Nonnegativity and lower semicontinuity at the finitely many points give the desired lower limit. This proves the comparison after smoothing and preserves the normalized Haar covolume.
sources: Tate, Fourier Analysis in Number Fields and Hecke's Zeta-Functions, Theorem 4.1.4, Lemmas 4.2.1–4.2.4 and the normalization following Theorem 4.2.1 <https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~alexk/2023S572/Tate1950.pdf>

literature.verdict: Unfolding for the proper left action of a countable discrete subgroup, with its counting measure and the ambient left Haar measure.
literature.comparison: Let G be second-countable, locally compact and Hausdorff, Γ a discrete subgroup, μ a left Haar measure and f:G→ℂ in L¹(μ). Subgroup.qms Γ μ is βμ on G for a cutoff with Σγ β(γg)=1. The periodization Σγ f(γg) is integrable for βμ and has integral ∫f dμ. The action of the countable discrete Γ on G is proper and preserves μ. Its normalized orbital integration is the proper-action instance of Gentner–Last §2, (2.5)–(2.9), since Γ is unimodular and its orbital measure counts along Γg. Any normalized cutoff gives the same integral of an orbit-invariant function by the change of variables g↦γg and inversion of the summation index. Apply first to |f| to obtain absolute convergence βμ-almost everywhere, then apply Fubini to the real and imaginary parts. A quotient by left cosets can equivalently carry the pushforward of βμ. The unfolding holds for nonunimodular G and for Γ of infinite covolume. Right-invariance of a measure on Γ\G is a separate property.

literature.verdict: Bruhat cells over a field are classical. An exact reference identifying these minors, unipotents and intermediate floor factors remains open.
literature.comparison: A is a field with involution and an element of trace one, and T.splitGram is invertible and Hermitian. For γ in its isometry group assume every leading minor of the frame Gram matrix is nonzero. For every floor j, including the default top floor ϱ, the theorem gives u,u′ in the Bessel unipotent, units p_i and σ in GT(j), with γ=u⁻¹w_j(p)σu′. The element w_j(p) exchanges the first j hyperbolic pairs with reciprocal conjugate scalings. GT(j) fixes the preceding pairs, and at the top the middle isometry group remains. Borel–Tits §5.15 decomposes the rational points of a connected reductive group into U(k)nU(k) and gives the product coordinates of each cell. Knapp gives the real Lie group version. To identify this exact result one still needs the field and form hypotheses for the relevant group, the frame-minor criterion selecting the cell and the truncation at each j for this particular Bessel radical. The source supplies the latter by successively eliminating hyperbolic pairs.

literature.comparison: For U(p,q), n=p+q≥1 and l=2λ regular of the specified parity, opposite-sign differences in λ are at least 500n³+10n⁵. literature.comparison: The ring here is the integral finite adèles of a CM field containing a primitive 5040th root. The pin produces an integral z with z−z* a unit. Thus conjugation cannot act trivially on the residue field at a nonsplit prime fixed by it, excluding ramification in the quadratic extension of the real subfield. At an unramified nonsplit place Wall's classification gives a unique unimodular lattice of each rank, hence a basis with identity Gram matrix. At a split pair the Hermitian pairing is an ordinary perfect pairing of free modules on the two factors, where one chooses dual bases. The local changes of basis and their inverses assemble in the product of the local integer rings. Equality of field discriminant classes alone would not imply integral equivalence at ramified dyadic places.

  (hi : ∀ k ∈ K, ∀ x, Φ₀ (↑k *ᵥ x) = Φ₀ x) (b : HasCompactSupport Φ₀) {α : E} (hα : star α = α)
  (hα' : ∀ v, 0 < (Φ v α).re) : let F (z : selfAdjoint _) := ∫ x,
    (ψf E ((2⁻¹ : E) * (z.1 * (star x ⬝ᵥ x - α))) : ℂ) ∂volume.withDensity (Φ₀ ·)
  let σ (h : Gf E κ) x := if star x ⬝ᵥ x = α then Φ₀ (h⁻¹.1.1 *ᵥ (x ·)) else 0
  (∀ h, Summable (σ h)) ∧ ((classSum stdRatPoints K fun h ↦ ↑(tsum (σ h)) : ℝ) : ℂ) =
  (classSum stdRatPoints K 1 * √√|NumberField.discr E| *
  ∏ v, π ^ card κ / (card κ - 1)! * (Φ v α).re ^ (card κ - 1) : ℝ) * ∫ z, F z := by
imports.text: (Siegel's formula, one vector.) Let E carry Weil data, κ finite with #κ ≥ 3, K an open compact subgroup (IsLevel) of the finite adelic unitary group, Φ₀ a locally constant compactly supported function on 𝔸_f^κ invariant under K, and α ∈ E with ᾱ = α and Re Φ_v(α) > 0 for every v. The relation to the literature is the second reader's (literature).

literature.verdict: Weil's mean-value identity on a nonzero index fiber, with the one-vector constants worked out in the formal source.
literature.comparison: Weil, §52, Theorem 5, equation (41), equates the probability-normalized mean of the rational representation sum at a specified index with the gauge-measure integral on that fiber. The unitary case has ε=1/2, so his convergence bound m>2n+4ε−2 gives m≥3 for one vector. Lean chooses the standard definite sum of m norms, a totally positive self-conjugate index, an open subgroup of the finite integral unitary group, and a nonnegative, locally constant, compactly supported level-invariant finite test function. The formal proof converts the normalized group average into the class sum multiplied by its total mass (lines 128–135). It uses its codifferent and Haar conventions to obtain |disc E|^{1/4} (111–123), and the real Gaussian/Fourier integrals give π^m α_v^{m−1}/(m−1)! at each infinite place (136–141). The remaining density is the finite adelic Fourier integral with the explicit factor 1/2 in its character. Equation (41) supplies the invariant mean identity. These displayed constants come from the coordinate computation in Lean.

imports.text: If μ is a right-invariant measure on a group of the section (a Haar measure: locally compact, second countable, Hausdorff) and ν is an s-finite right-invariant measure, then ν = d·μ for some d ∈ [0, ∞]. The relation to the literature is the second reader's (literature).

literature.verdict: The full s-finite assertion extends regular Haar uniqueness and includes an infinite multiplier. There is a direct derivation from s-finite Tonelli.
literature.comparison: On a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group G, fix a left Haar measure μ also invariant on the right. Every s-finite right-invariant Borel measure ν satisfies ν=dμ for d∈[0,∞]. The zero measure and ∞·μ are both allowed. For comparison, van Doorn §6, Theorem 12, following Halmos, assumes regular invariant measures and normalizes on a compact set of finite positive Haar measure. Ordinary uniqueness for locally finite Haar measures alone cannot cover ∞·μ. The s-finite extension follows with a compactly supported nonnegative φ of μ-integral 1. For nonnegative measurable f consider ∫∫ f(x)φ(xy⁻¹)dμ(y)dν(x). Left invariance and inversion invariance of the bi-invariant μ give ∫f dν. Staton Proposition 5 permits interchanging the integrals. Substituting x=zy by right invariance of ν and integrating f(zy) over μ yields (∫φ dν)(∫f dμ), including the extended scalar conventions. Take f to be each measurable indicator. A Bourbaki statement explicitly allowing an s-finite ν and d=∞ was not located.

literature.verdict: Finite sums of pairwise orthogonal central idempotents for the restricted Green labels
literature.comparison: For the same finite family of fields and finite matrix index, s is any finite set of polynomial tuples. Each invalid tuple contributes zero. For two distinct valid tuples some local polynomials differ, hence a factor has disjoint Green character parameter. Orthogonality kills the product of the corresponding central idempotents. Their tensor products remain orthogonal and summing gives the two fields of IsCentralProj: idempotence and conjugacy-invariant coefficients. The assertion alone cannot recover irreducibility or classify characters. The empty sum and nonlabel terms are allowed. Self-adjointness is a separate consequence of the coefficient formula.
sources: J. A. Green, The characters of the finite general linear groups, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1955), §8, Theorems 13–14, pp. 441–444, especially Theorem 14 and the degree formula on pp. 443–444. The parameters assign a partition to each Frobenius orbit of multiplicative characters. <https://www.ams.org/tran/1955-080-02/S0002-9947-1955-0072878-2/S0002-9947-1955-0072878-2.pdf#page=42>
